label: Phase 8i audit: memory-budget violation, root cause and fix (no protected labels used)

violations.why_missed: watchdog sampled the CURRENT working set every 5 s; both peaks were shorter

root_cause.window_build: full captures were read in one-hour slices by repeated lazy Polars scans (scan_parquet(...).filter(hour).collect()); process memory grew with every scan while nothing was held

evidence_nfton_dev.frozen_build_trace: working set rose ~40 MiB per 500k-row slice to 2.2 GB working set / 2.7 GB commit

nfbot_specific_metadata_only.note: timestamps and Parquet metadata only; no labels read. Overlapping row groups mean each hourly scan decoded many groups; the 4.05M-flow hour was the largest slice

ruled_out.slice_collect_alone: 0.78M-flow hourly collect on NF-ToN-IoT: +41 MiB working set
ruled_out.distinct_destinations: NF-BoT-IoT-v3 has 291 destination addresses, NF-ToN-IoT 8,777: the destination sets are negligible
ruled_out.string_view_retention: per-process test: no consistent difference between rechunk/shrink and none
ruled_out.concurrent_processes: builds ran alone (watchdog and shell only)

root_cause.ingest: the CSV block size sets the peak: NF-UNSW-NB15-v3 ingest, 64 MiB blocks 1922 MiB working set (2223 MiB commit), 16 MiB blocks 993 MiB (1233 MiB commit), identical output

fix.window_build: slices of at most 500,000 flows cut on the 30 s window grid; each slice read one Parquet row group at a time and filtered at once (scripts/phase8i/build_windows.py)
fix.enforcement: scripts/run_capped.py: Windows Job Object on total committed memory (OS-enforced; allocations past the cap fail), exact PeakJobMemoryUsed recorded; watchdog now reads the per-process PEAK working set

validation_synthetic_bot_shaped.workload: 10.55M synthetic flows, 20 sources, 290 destinations, a 4.05M-flow hour, ~300k-row groups unsorted within each hour

cost: the bounded reader re-reads overlapping row groups: NF-CIC and NF-ToN-IoT builds take 1.9-2.5x longer
